findings.body:
**Authorization removed from a destructive endpoint.** Dropping `@require_role("admin")` leaves `DELETE /users/<user>` callable by anyone; any client that can reach the app can delete arbitrary users (`USERS.remove(user)` → 204).

Cleanup jobs hitting 403 should get a proper principal (service account / admin credentials) or a dedicated, authenticated internal path — not an open delete handler.

If the 403s came from `require_role` checking the path `user` instead of the caller, fix the decorator to read the authenticated identity; do not remove the guard.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical authorization bypass: this PR removes the only access control on `DELETE /users/<user>`, so any caller can delete any user.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `app.py:19` | Removes `@require_role("admin")` from user deletion, leaving the destructive endpoint unauthenticated |

## Notes

`require_role` itself appears to check the *path* `user` against `ROLES` rather than an authenticated caller identity, so cleanup-job 403s may be a decorator bug (wrong principal) rather than a reason to drop the check. The right fix is to authorize the *caller* (e.g. service account / admin role on the job identity) and keep the endpoint protected.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
